title: Charts as a Hazel library over the HTML substrate
body:
Charts, without bundling a charting library into Hazel.

Replaces the d3-backed chart projector in #2350 (which this supersedes — that
approach put the whole chart vocabulary inside the implementation, so every new
chart kind, scale, or annotation was an OCaml change *plus* a JS change, and
`ChartProj` could not be tested at all because its output only existed inside
d3's DOM).

Here there is no `Chart` type and no chart projector. A chart is an ordinary
`HTML` value built from this branch's `Node` and `Create` escape hatches (which
render SVG), and the charting vocabulary — scales, nice-domain rounding, tick
selection, axes, bands, arcs, legends, palette — is Hazel source in
`hazel-programs/charts/charts.hz` that a reader can fork. Adding a stacked bar
or a log scale is a change to Hazel code. No d3, no npm additions.

### What the implementation gains instead

Not chart knowledge — a way to draw *values*:

- **`HtmlRenderer`**, a rich probe (`^^probe_html`), renders a probe sample as
  whatever its value describes: static HTML as DOM, or an
  `(init, update, view, subs)` 4-tuple as a running app keyed on the probe's id.
  This is what a computed chart needs — `Chart.bar(sales)` is an application, so
  its HTML only exists after evaluation. It is the value-side counterpart to
  `HTMLProj`, and mirrors its two commit modes.

  When the probed expression is *itself* html, a handler commits by **rewriting
  the source** to `f(H)` and letting the program's own pipeline evaluate it —
  splicing the handler by the name the evaluator recorded on it, so the edit
  lands on the definition and every call sees it. Evaluating the transform inside
  the renderer cannot work: a probe has no elaborated syntax and no environment
  to resolve `f` in.

- ~~**`View.docked`** lets a projector send a secondary surface to the Projectors
  panel while keeping its inline presence — distinct from
  `ProjectorCore.Placement`, which moves the whole projector and leaves a chip.
  `ProbeProj` owns rich-probe placement, so every renderer docks with no
  per-renderer support, `TableRenderer` included.~~

  Dropped. `hazel-html` had meanwhile answered the same question — where an open
  rich probe draws — with `drawer_mode`, `auto_rich`/`rich_off` and a `below`
  slot, opening the drawer when content exceeds `inline_rows_cap`. Two designs
  for one concern, so this branch took upstream's: `renderer_placement`,
  `ToggleRendererPlacement`, the `docked` slot, `ProjectorView.docked_views` and
  the panel's docked-probe pass are all gone. Nothing else needed changing —
  `renderer_placement` had no consumers outside `ProbeProj`.

  What is *not* a competing design is the chart work itself: `HtmlRenderer` stays
  registered beside upstream's `CardRenderer`, and gained the two members
  `hazel-html` added to the renderer signature — `auto_applies` (HTML and MVU
  apps are real evidence, so `true`) and `drawer_rows` (arbitrary-height UI, so
  above `inline_rows_cap` and drawer-bound).

- **`project_html`** (Nut menu → HTML) renders an HTML-valued result in the
  evaluation output, mirroring the existing Tables toggle and off by default.
  Gated on the constructor's *type* rather than its name, and projects only the
  outermost node — every child of an element is itself an HTML constructor
  application, so projecting each one would wrap a projector around every element
  in the tree.

### Slides

Four, under **Charts**:

| Slide | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Charts | The `Svg`/`Scale`/`Chart` library plus a gallery of all five kinds |
| Linked Views | Drag a bar; a pie derived inside `view` follows |
| Table Explorer | One row-polymorphic app over two B2T2 tables |
| Steps | A probe inside a recursion — one sample per step — and html that edits its own source |

Table Explorer reuses B2T2's `Student` / `GradebookEntry` tables and the
idiomatic `groupByRetentive` from `table-api-utilities-groupbyretentive.hz`, so
the app is driven by the real table API. Steps is the pair of things a probe can
do that a projector cannot: record *many* samples, and stay additive so the
source it draws is still on screen and still typeable.

### Also here

- **`27577e6122` fixes a bug on this branch** (see the review comments on
  `Ascriptions.re`): annotating a parameter with a builtin recursive alias
  (`HTML`, `JSON`, `Cmd`, `Sub`) made `case` on that argument silently stop
  reducing. `compact_builtin_recs` leaves those aliases compact (`Var("HTML")`)
  and `Typ.unroll` doesn't resolve a `Var`, so the two constructor guards never
  matched and the ascription never pushed in. Bisected to `bce50ac5fc`; widened
  to `JSON` by the dev merge `b18b27d8bd`. **That commit is cherry-pickable on
  its own** if you'd rather take it directly.
- `simple_icon` hoisted into `SvgUtil`; `Icons` and `TableRenderer` each had a
  copy, since haz3lcore can't depend on web.
- `HTMLProj.init` now sees through `Parens`, which auto-display needs in order to
  get the single piece a projector replaces.
- `docs/charts.md` covers the three-layer split, the projector-vs-probe
  distinction, and the traps — including why evaluate-and-splice is the wrong
  way to edit source from a probe.

### Tests

`Test_Charts` asserts on the value tree the library produces, including that
grouped series align by label rather than position (the fix from #2350's review),
the degenerate cases, and the scale/tick arithmetic. Plus `Test_HtmlRenderer`,
`ExpToSegment.ProjectHtml` (one projector at the root, not one per element), and
two regression tests for the `Ascriptions` fix in `Test_Evaluator_Sum_Types`.

Based on `hazel-html`, so it needs #2115 to land first. Merged with `hazel-html`
at ~~`33e0053fb8`~~ `f21ac5f8dd`.

title: Split the B2T2 slides per operation, in line with the current benchmark
body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Needs a second opinion on one thing:** commit 1 switches `MenhirCorpus` from
> `Parser.to_zipper` to `Parser.to_segment`, and I am **not confident that is safe
> in general** — only that it holds across today's corpus. See
> "[The part I'm unsure about](#the-part-im-unsure-about)". The slide split
> (commit 2) is independent and can land without it.

## What

**Splits the B2T2 slides per operation, bringing them in line with the current
version of the benchmark.** The committed slides grouped several categories into
one file each — `Aggregate`, `Subtable`, `Properties`, `Ordering`,
`MissingValues`, `DataCleaning`, `AccessSubcomponents`, and the three Errors
"parts" — while the artifact's lab sources keep one file per operation. This
regenerates `hazel-programs/docs/b2t2` from those sources: **39 files → 62**, one
slide per operation, and picks up the upstream slide edits along with the split.

The menu therefore goes from 39 to 62 entries. That's the user-visible part of
this PR and the bit worth an opinion.

Names and menu order come from the manifest in `sync-slides.sh` (B2T2 operation
order, not alphabetical). The 28 slides that were already one-per-operation keep
their existing filenames, so the churn is limited to the 10 grouped files and the
33 replacing them.

## Why it also makes the suite much faster

The grouped files were the largest programs in the corpus — `table-api-aggregate.hz`
alone was 10.5 KB — and the editor parser is superlinear: `to_segment` only splits
at top-level boundaries, so within a segment cost still grows faster than linearly.
Re-splitting the same content (largest file now 6.7 KB, total bytes essentially
unchanged) cut `MarkerParse.of_text` over the corpus by **39%** and
`Parser.to_segment` by **32%**.

So this is faster while testing *more*: the suite gains 69 cases, because 62
slides generate more per-slide checks than 39 did.

| group | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `MenhirCorpus` | 90.4 s | 21.2 s |
| `DocSlides.ReparseBackuptext` | 52.7 s | 11.7 s |
| `TextRoundtrip.DocSlides` | 103.4 s | 78.0 s |
| **full suite (local)** | **345.5 s** | **211.0 s** (−38.9%) |
| test cases | 3496 | 3565 |

Measured locally with a `junit_alcotest` patched to record real per-case times —
upstream hardcodes `~time:0.`, which is why none of this was visible from the
existing reports.

## Commit 1: the test-side parse changes

Two changes, independent of the slide split:

**`MenhirCorpus` parses via `to_segment` instead of `to_zipper`** (90.4 s → 37.2 s
on the old corpus). See the warning below.

**`MenhirCorpus` and `DocSlides.ReparseBackuptext` share the parse.** They turn out
to check the same programs — the corpus files *are* the slide sources — and both
need the typing parser's segment, which each was paying for separately.
`test/ParsedCorpus.re` memoizes it, taking `ReparseBackuptext` from 51.7 s to
11.5 s. Making the cache hit required `MenhirCorpus` to normalize the way the load
path does (dedent every line, strip one trailing newline) rather than
`String.trim`, since otherwise the two callers key different strings for the same
program. That drops the indented-form differential — narrow, and a shape
production never produces, since every slide is dedented on load.

Worth recording that the original hypothesis here was wrong: the two *slide*
groups looked redundant, but `DocSlides` spends its time in `MarkerParse.of_text`
and `ReparseBackuptext` in `Parser.to_segment`, and the one call they share costs
about a tenth of a second. The real duplication was with `MenhirCorpus`.

## The part I'm unsure about

`Parser.to_zipper` is the **definitional** editor parse — it replays what the
editor does per keystroke. `Parser.to_segment` is an *optimization* over it: it
splits the input at points it believes are safe, strips the convex grout artifact
`Zipper.init()` leaves behind, then does a final top-level regrout to reconcile
shapes across boundaries. Any of those three steps could plausibly differ from
to_zipper for a program shape not in today's corpus.

**What I did verify**, because it's the failure mode that would hide itself:
`check_file` silently passes when the editor parser returns `None`, so a file that
`to_segment` rejected would have dropped out of coverage with the suite still
green. That does not happen — across all corpus files both entry points accept
every file and produce structurally equal terms.

**What I did not verify** is that the two agree in general. The consequence is
that `MenhirCorpus` now pins menhir against the optimized parser rather than the
ground-truth one, so if `to_segment` ever drifts from `to_zipper`, this test would
compare against the wrong baseline and not notice.

The invariant "`to_segment` ≡ `to_zipper` corpus-wide" is worth asserting, but
doing so costs about what using `to_zipper` here would, which is the entire saving
— so it belongs in a periodic run rather than per-PR. That's noted in the file's
header. **If reviewers would rather not take this on faith, commit 1's swap can be
dropped and the shared-parse half kept; the slide split carries most of the win
regardless.**

## `known_gaps` fallout, which is an improvement

The single `table-api-properties.hz` gap entry was tolerating three operations at
once. Split, the `[()]` tokenizer quirk turns out to affect `header` and `ncols`
but **not** `nrows` — so the ledger now names the two files that actually carry it,
and `nrows` is genuinely checked for the first time. No new gaps.

## Verified

- `make dev` builds the web bundle against the regenerated `Slides.re`
- full suite green
- `MenhirCorpus` green with the re-attributed ledger

## Not addressed here

`TextRoundtrip.DocSlides` is now the largest remaining group at 78 s, all of it in
`MarkerParse.of_text` → `to_zipper`. Reimplementing that over `to_segment` is worth
roughly 40 s more, but it is production code (`PersistentZipper`'s fallback path),
needs a zipper rather than a segment, and also strips implicit holes and preserves
refractors — a real refactor rather than a substitution, so it is deliberately out
of scope.

Separately: the `unused open EditingPrelude` warning in `Test_ReparseDocSlides.re`
is untouched here. Its removal belongs to #2456, on #2422.

title: Fix: retain probes when fast-parsing almost-complete syntax
body:
the menhir fast parse path supports complete and almost-complete terms... specifically it supports things that would be terms if a hole was inserted at the end. however, fast-parsing such almost-complete things currently loses probes.

eg say a `.hz`  file ends in a semicolon:

```
let f = fun x -> x + 1 in
^^probe(f(1));
^^probe(f(2));
```

this loads with both probes attached but reprints without them, so `./hazel format` and any save of a loaded-but-unedited buffer destroy the probes.

Cause: menhir rejects the dangling `;`, FastParse's append-a-hole retry strips the hole it added, and loading was the one path into the editor that doesn't regrout,  so the buffer ends in an operand-less `;`, `Segment.skel` fails on it, and `Triggers.refractor_seg_to_seg` gives up and reprints the program without its `^^probe(...)` wrappers (invocations nested inside tile children survive, which is why body-less let chains usually looked fine).

Fix: `PersistentZipper.parse_text` regrouts after unzip, same as every edit. Saving such a fragment spells the materialized hole (`...f(2));¿`) and is a fixed point thereafter.

closes #2450

title: Fix: menhir treats () as an atomic pattern (editor parity)
body:
`fun () : T -> e`, `fun x :: () -> e`, and `fun (), x -> x` were menhir parse errors the editor parser accepts. The editor treats `()` as an atomic pattern; the menhir grammar listed UNIT at hand-picked parameter positions and every unlisted one was a gap. Final commit makes UNIT an atomic pattern (nonAscriptingPat) and deletes the positional special cases. 8 pins in Test_Menhir; MenhirParser/MenhirFuzz/FastParse/FastParseCorpus/MenhirCorpus green.

Pinning surfaced a pre-existing divergence parked as a skip case: on `fun x :: y : [T] ->` MakeTerm ascribes the last element, menhir the whole chain, needs its own decision.

title: FastParse: weave nested triggers
body:
`^^probe(^^slider(50))` bailed the fast path (`token 5: segment has '50', source has '^^slider'`): inside `consume_trigger`, `grab` wove the wrapped pieces with `weave_piece`, which is trigger-blind. This factors the two trigger arms of `weave_seg` into a shared `weave_trigger` that `grab` now tries first, so triggers nest. The regression test asserts the fast path itself handles the nest (no silent fallback), that the pin is collected and the wrapped projector materializes, and that the load path reprints the source verbatim.

Fixes #2447

title: Add .rei interfaces for 13 leaf modules
body:
Same mechanism as the previous PR, applied to leaf modules — ones with only one or
two callers. These had no interface, so every internal helper was exported to all
485 modules in the build. Declaring just the surface used across files removes
**267 values from the public API for 24 declarations**, in 213 lines.

The public set came from the `ocaml-index` occurrence data — a value is public iff
some occurrence lies in another file — not from grep, so it is the same data
`scripts/find_dead_code.py` already reasons about.

| module | now private | declared |
|---|--:|--:|
| `DebugSidebar` | 47 | 1 |
| `TyDiForms` | 35 | 3 |
| `ContextMenu` | 31 | 3 |
| `CursorInspector` | 30 | 5 |
| `Abbreviate` | 27 | 2 |
| `CustomStatics` | 24 | 2 |
| `SampleFocusBar` | 16 | 1 |
| `Sidebar` | 14 | 1 |
| `SlashCommandOutputView` | 12 | 1 |
| `CompositionPrompt` | 11 | 1 |
| `WorkerMessagingSection` | 11 | — |
| `ProbeText` | 10 | 2 |
| `EdgeScroll` | 10 | 2 |

`DebugSidebar.rei` is two lines and seals 47 values, which is the general shape
here: leaf modules expose one `view` and everything else was incidental.

`WorkerMessagingSection.rei` is just `include DebugSection.S;` — that moves its
contract check from the `(module ...)` pack site in `DebugSidebar.re:751` to the
definition itself.

## No dead code turned up, and that's the expected result

Warning 32 is a hard error under `--profile release`, so a clean build is positive
confirmation that all 267 values are used internally. `src/` remains at the
detector's fixpoint. Unlike the util PR — where `Tree.equal_struct` fell out —
there was nothing left to find here.

## Two things the interfaces surfaced, documented rather than fixed

- **`CustomStatics.custom_statics_deferred_ap` discards `~ancestors`**, and its one
  caller (`Statics.re:1751`) passes a bare pun that resolves to `unit`, where all
  eight other `ancestors` call sites in that file pass `ancestors_inclusive`. I
  tried annotating the parameter `list(Id.t)` to match its two siblings and it does
  not compile. Harmless while the parameter is discarded; a trap if anyone ever
  reads it. Deciding what it *should* receive is a semantic call, so the `.rei`
  records the situation instead.
- **`Abbreviate.AbbrevBudget.split_evenly` is exported only because
  `Test_Abbreviate` covers it directly** — no `src/` caller. Noted in the interface
  so it is not mistaken for production API.

## Verification

`dune build @src/fmt src --profile release` and `make dev` both clean.

The seals were checked rather than assumed: referencing `DebugSidebar.toggle_bar`
and `Abbreviate.AbbrevBudget.with_budget` from outside now fails with
`Unbound value`, covering both the top-level and nested-module cases.

title: Add .rei interfaces for 12 src/util modules
body:
Without an interface, every top-level binding in a module is exported, so the
compiler can never tell you one is unused. Adding a `.rei` turns warning 32 back
on — and it is a hard error under `--profile release`, which
`deploy_branches.yml:69` gates on. So for these 12 modules, unused code now fails
CI instead of accumulating.

Each interface declares only the module's real external surface, so anything used
solely inside its own file becomes private. `JsUtil` alone hides 12 helpers
(`date_now`, `find_scroll_container`, `QueryParams.get_arguments`, …).

264 lines of interface, 23 of them restated types.

## Which 12

Picked by how many lines of type declaration you would have to maintain in two
places — not by file size:

`ListUtil` 64 · `JsUtil` 60 · `StringUtil` 27 · `Unicode` 25 · `Tree` 23 ·
`OptUtil` 19 · `Aba` 18 · `VarMap` 9 · `StructureShareSexp` 8 · `Direction` 5 ·
`Either` 4 · `FloatingElement` 2

## What's excluded

- **`Menu` (70 restated type lines) and `OpenRouter` (101).** Inline
  `module M: { … } = { … }` sealing gets the same coverage with the signature
  written once. `Id.re:142` already does it that way.
- **`include <third-party>` modules** — `BigInt`, `Sets`, `Maps`, `MapUtil`,
  `IntMap`, `Result`. `BigInt` is 14 source lines and extracts to 184; `refmt`
  cannot parse it. Such an interface is a hand-copy of someone else's API that
  breaks on their next release.
- **`Util.re`**, which dune treats as the library interface module.

## It found two dead functions immediately

`Tree.equal_struct`, and then `Tree.equal` once that went. **The index-based
detector could not see either** — both match its `^equal` ppx-name suppression,
which exists because ppx-generated call sites do not appear in the index at all.
Worth knowing that the two tools miss different things.

## Tooling

`scripts/gen_rei.sh` / `make rei FILE=...` generates a starter interface:
`ocamlc -i` over the ppx-expanded source dune already built, piped through
`refmt`. Output is refmt-clean so `@src/fmt` accepts it. It strips the library's
own alias prefix, since `-short-paths` renders siblings as `Util.Either.t`, which
is a dependency cycle inside `src/util`.

One gotcha if you write one by hand: **a `.rei` can declare fewer derivers than
the `.re` and still compile**, because the ppx wraps generated values in
`[@@@ocaml.warning "-32"]`. That drift only surfaces as `Unbound value` at a
consumer. Structural drift is caught immediately.

## Verification

`make test-quick`: 3,225 passing. dev, test and release builds clean — release is
the one that matters, since dev will not fail on the unused values a new interface
exposes.

title: Delete dead stylesheets, CSS rules, and unreferenced image assets
body:
26 files, **−1,640 lines**. **No compiler can check any of this**, so the liveness
argument matters more than the diff. Three commits, each using a progressively
stronger test.

## 1. Three whole stylesheets

- **`assistant.css` (833 lines)** — every rule is scoped under `#assistant`, and
  nothing renders `id="assistant"`. The sidebar's HelpfulAssistant panel renders
  `AgentView.view` (`Sidebar.re:340`), styled by `style/agent/*.css`, which is
  where every class the agent UI actually uses (`send-button`,
  `message-container`, `message-identifier`, `llm-identifier`, `dot1`, …) is
  defined. The only unscoped rules — `.llm-selector`/`.llm-label`/`.llm-dropdown`
  — are unreferenced in source.
- **`project.css` (315 lines)** — styles a projects/file-system UI that no longer
  exists. All five ids and 18 of 20 classes have zero source references; the other
  two are generic (`.cell`, `.icon`) matched only as descendants of the dead ids.
- **`agent.css`** — empty file, imported nowhere.

## 2. Individual rules, judged by source grep

22 rule blocks across 9 stylesheets, 12 unreferenced icons, and
`style/palette.html` (a design swatch page nothing links to and no dune rule
copies into the build).

The test is deliberately over-cautious. A selector counts as **live** if any of:

- its name appears as a string literal anywhere in `src/` or `test/`;
- **some literal is a prefix of it**, since classes get concatenated —
  `"depth-" ++ string_of_int n`, `"agent-md-h" ++ string_of_int level`,
  `"highlight-code-" ++ c`, `"slash-card-" ++ kind`;
- **its name appears as a bare OCaml token.** `Sort` and `cls` constructors reach
  the DOM through `show`/`to_string` and never appear as a literal at all — that
  is `.Mod`, `.Sig`, `.MPat`, `.Rul`, `.EmptyHole`, `.Single`. A naive
  literals-only scan called all of those dead.

That took the candidate list from 72 names to 22, each then re-checked by hand for
both hyphenated and underscored spellings.

A rule is removed only when **every** comma-separated selector is dead, judged by
the key (rightmost) compound: `.projector.probe .window-toggle` can only match an
element carrying `.window-toggle`, so it goes even though `.projector` is live.
Rules whose key compound is an element selector are left alone
(`.step-back:hover span` survives) — which leaves a few orphans but cannot break
anything.

## 3. The stronger test: grep the compiled bundle

If a class name appears nowhere in the 11 MB `hazel.js`, no code path can put it
on an element, so any rule naming it is unreachable. Controls confirm the test
discriminates rather than trivially passing: `projector` 108 hits, `probe` 256,
`hsod` 9, `depth-` 4, `highlight-code-` 1, `agent-md-h` 3.

Ten classes still defined in CSS can never be emitted, and their rules go:
`developer-notes-display`, `view-icon-button`, `deselected`, `call-cursor`,
`click-kbd-pill`, `is-index`, `qr-when-unfocused`, `window-toggle`, `step-back`,
`step-expand`. Nine are ones commit 2 deliberately spared for having an element
key selector — unreachable all the same, since nothing carries `.step-back`.

**`call-cursor` is a correction.** Commit 2 kept it because `call_cursor` exists in
source — but that is a function name; the hyphenated class is never emitted. The
source-grep test was wrong there and the bundle test is right. That is the honest
summary of why there are two commits instead of one.

Where a rule mixed dead and live selectors, only the dead branches are dropped:
`.prompt-display, .developer-notes-display` keeps `.prompt-display`. One such trim
initially took the rule's leading comment with it, because the dead branch was
listed first and carried the preceding trivia — restored.

## Browser verification

Done, and it covers all three commits: probe sidebar (including
`#sample-focus-bar` with a focused sample, and probe hover cards with kbd badges),
agent panel, agent main menu, nut menu, editor context menu, stepper (took a
step), tutorial mode (completed a step, checkmark renders), exercises mode with
grading reports, and the projectors slide. No console errors, no unstyled surfaces.

If you re-verify: **restart the browser rather than hard-reloading** — a stale Web
Worker survives a reload and reports `EXN:TypeError reading '1'` from eval, which
looks like a real regression and is not.

`licenses/Icons.md` is a blanket Noun Project attribution rather than per-icon, so
removing unused icons does not affect it.

title: Deduplicate three copy-pasted implementations
body:
Eight files, +145/−308. Three independent de-duplications, one per commit. Unlike
the rest of the stack these *change* code rather than delete it, so each commit
carries an argument for why the surviving version is equivalent.

## 1. Grading primitives and the SVG icon helper

`Grading.re` documents itself as the shared primitives module and
`CodeGrading.re` does `include Grading;`. **`TutorialGrading.re` did not** — it
re-declared `type percentage`/`points`/`score`, `score_of_percent`, `score_view`
and `percentage_view` verbatim, down to the `Printf` format strings. Replaced with
`include Grading;`, which also picks up `pending_score_view`, the one primitive it
had not copied.

Separately, `icon_size`/`simple_icon` were byte-identical in `Icons.re` (web) and
`TableRenderer.re` (haz3lcore). `haz3lcore` cannot depend on `web`, so it had been
retyped. Hoisted into `Util.SvgUtil`, which both libraries reach and which already
opens `Virtual_dom`.

## 2. Point `Tutorial.re` at `EditorUtil.append_exp`

`append_exp` existed three times. `EditorUtil.re` is canonical; `CodeExercise`'s
copy was already dead and went in the preceding branch; `Tutorial`'s was the last
live duplicate.

**Verified equivalent rather than assumed**, because the two built annotations
differently:

| | Tutorial | EditorUtil |
|---|---|---|
| base case | `IdTag.fresh()` | `IdTag.mk([Haz3lcore.Id.mk()], empty_secondary)` |
| recursive | `IdTag.mk_internal(ids(e1))` | `IdTag.mk(ids(e1), empty_secondary)` |

`IdTagged.re:36-47` makes `mk_internal(ids)` structurally equal to
`mk(ids, empty_secondary)`, and `fresh()` equal to
`{ids: [Id.mk()], secondary: empty_secondary}`.

The remaining question was whether `Haz3lcore.Id.mk` and the `Id.mk` resolved
inside `IdTagged.re` are the same generator — **there are three modules named `Id`
in this repo.** Both `src/language/Id.re` and `src/haz3lcore/Id.re` are
`include Util.Id;`, so they share the one `Uuidm.v4_gen` closure.

Constructor coverage is also identical: both dispatch recursively on exactly
`Seq`, `Filter`, `Let`, `Theorem`, `TyAlias` and `Use`, and both put the same 41
constructors in the catch-all — including `ModuleExp`, which an earlier copy
handled recursively.

## 3. Functorize `SliderProj` / `SliderFProj`

63 lines each, 52 identical — the entire difference was `Bigint` vs `float`: which
atom they read, which atom they build, how they render. `SliderCore.Make` now holds
the shared body and each variant supplies only that difference, 14-16 lines apiece.

`Atom.t` is the natural seam: both were matching `Exp({term: Atom(Int(i)), _})` /
`Atom(Float(f))` and rebuilding the same way, so `PARAMS` asks for
`of_atom`/`to_atom`/`to_string` and nothing else.

Net −17 lines, which undersells it — the point is that a change to slider
behaviour is now one edit rather than two that can drift apart.

Failure message wording is preserved (`"Slider: Get: not integer literal"`,
`"SliderF: Put: not float literal"`) via a separate `literal` label rather than
being degraded to the module name. `ProjectorInit.re:12-13` references
`SliderProj.M`/`SliderFProj.M` and is unchanged.

## Verification

`make test-quick`: 3,225 passing. dev, test and release builds clean.

Both sliders were also exercised by hand in the browser — dragged each, and the
cursor inspector read `Projector (Slider) : Int` and `Projector (SliderF) : Float`.
That check matters here because a functor that typechecks can still be wired to the
wrong literal, and no test covers projector interaction.

title: Delete dead code, to a fixpoint
body:
176 files, **−5,589 lines**, +16. **Worth reading commit-by-commit rather than as
a single diff** — the commits are deliberately ordered so each is independently
checkable, and squashing them together makes the reasoning impossible to follow.

| area | files | removed |
|---|--:|--:|
| `src/web` | 52 | −1,678 |
| `src/language` | 38 | −1,213 |
| `src/haz3lcore` | 35 | −1,058 |
| `src/pretty` | 14 | −880 |
| `src/util` | 20 | −607 |
| `test` | 13 | −119 |
| `src/CLI`, `src/menhirParser`, dune/opam | 4 | −34 |

## Kept at reviewer request

Review round 1 did exactly what the PR asked for — people recognised things they
wanted. **19 definitions across 12 files are restored** in "Restore definitions
reviewers asked to keep". They are listed here rather than tracked by the
detector, so this table is the record: `make dead-code` reports every one of them
again, by design.

| restored | file | asked by | reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `err_msg` | `language/term/InvalidOperationError.re` | @Negabinary | "wanna use it shortly" |
| `fresh` | `language/term/MPat.re` | @Negabinary | `MPat` was the only term module missing one |
| `temp` ×3 | `language/term/{Sig,Mod,MPat}.re` | @Negabinary | same — three had lost it, not one |
| `print_timestamp` | `util/JsUtil.re` | @Negabinary | "don't want to look up how to do this again" |
| `print_time_prefix`, `print_time`, `print_times`, `measure_time` | `util/TimeUtil.re` | @Negabinary | "looks useful" |
| `Debug` | `haz3lcore/projectors/implementations/ProbeProj.re` | @disconcision | "would prefer to keep this" |
| `empty`, `listlit_lbl`, `mod_lbl` | `haz3lcore/lang/Token.re` | @disconcision | used in #2389 |
| `sorted_children` | `haz3lcore/tiles/Tile.re` | @disconcision | used in #2374 |
| `abbreviate_pat` | `language/term/Abbreviate.re` | @disconcision | used in #2115 |
| `shard_index` | `haz3lcore/zipper/action/Indicated.re` | @disconcision | used in #1959 |
| `to_actions` | `web/app/Log.re` | @Negabinary | wanted by the log-replay work |
| `exercise` ×3 | `web/exercises/examples/Blank*Exercise.ml` | @Negabinary | **these are templates** — see below |

The `Blank*Exercise.ml` files are the one place the sweep was simply wrong. They
were hollowed out rather than deleted, leaving a nine-line header that ends
*"…and edit the arguments below"* with nothing below it. They are unreferenced
**by design**, in the same way as the entry-point files the detector already
exempts — a template nobody has instantiated yet has no callers and never will.

## If you wanted something here, say so

The detector finds definitions with **no recorded reference**. It cannot tell rot
from:

- an API deliberately built out ahead of its callers,
- an escape hatch kept around for debugging,
- work someone has in progress on another branch and hasn't wired up yet.

All three look identical to "dead". Round 1 caught the items above; if there is
more, a comment on the relevant commit is enough, and everything here is
recoverable from git history.

## The commits

1. **Delete the dead `src/pretty` library.** 866 lines, 14 modules, zero
   references anywhere — no `Pretty.*` use, no `open Pretty`. The apparent hits
   are `PrettySegment`, an unrelated module in `haz3lcore`. It stayed compiled
   only because `src/web/dune` listed it in `(libraries)`. Removing it also drops
   **the 12 `Obj.magic` calls in `MeasuredLayout`/`Box`/`LayoutOfDoc` — the only
   ones in the repo outside js_of_ocaml DOM interop** — and
   `src/pretty/{ListUtil,Unicode}.re`, which duplicated `src/util` verbatim
   because the library declared no `(libraries)` and so could not see it.

2. **Empty files, orphan modules, commented-out code.** Two 1-byte files;
   `ReadTools.re` (115 lines, never wired into `CompositionUtils.re`'s tool list
   while its six siblings have 3-18 references each); `LogEntry`, `FailedInput`,
   `ExerciseUtil`; and 57 consecutive commented-out lines in `CodeGrading.re`.

3. **111 unused top-level definitions.** Largest: `RuleImage.of_sort` (133
   lines), `API.node_request_streaming` (81), `Indentation.go'` (46). Densest:
   `Icons.re` (11 unused SVG icons, including `add_file`/`add_folder`/
   `add_project` from the removed projects UI).

4. **Dead code exposed by the previous sweep**, to a fixpoint: 8 more in round
   two, 1 in round three, 0 in round four. Notably `Sidebar.switch_assistant`,
   whose only caller was the old assistant tab handler.

5. **Dead definitions found by the index**, to a fixpoint: 3,769 lines across 134
   files. This is the category the text scan structurally could not see — 58
   members nested inside `module X = {...}` blocks, and functions whose only
   callers are their own recursive calls (`Segment.remold_sig_uni`,
   `CodeExercise.append_exp`, `ValueChecker.check_value_mod_ctx`).

6. **Dead types, constructors and write-only record fields** — the category the
   index cannot see *at all*, because `[@deriving]` emits ghost occurrences for
   every constructor at the type declaration. Found by hand, each checked
   individually. Includes `SafeTriangle.active_state`'s
   `exit_point`/`menu_direction`, which are written in `activate` and never read;
   warning 69 cannot see this because they *are* written.

7. **`OptUtil.filter`**, restored — it became live on `dev` while this branch was
   open.

8. **Restore definitions reviewers asked to keep** — the 19 above, plus four
   dangling comments left behind by earlier deletions (`Typ.re`, `API.re`,
   `TutorialGrading.re`, and an over-long rationale in
   `Test_Evaluator_Properties.re`).

## What was deliberately not deleted

The part I would most like scrutinised, because it is where judgement replaced
mechanism.

- **Anything a ppx can synthesise a call to** without it appearing in source:
  `Sample.{show,sexp_of,…}_targets`, `RichProbe.show_packed_*`,
  `RichProbeRegistry.yojson_of_packed_action`, `ConstructorMap.equal_constructor`,
  `Tree.equal_struct`. `Sample.re`'s are reached from `EvalInfo.re`'s
  `[@deriving sexp]` on a `Sample.targets` field.
- **Comment blocks that carry knowledge rather than rot**: the `pp` overrides in
  `Annotated.re`/`IdTagged.re` are documented debugging affordances;
  `ProofRule.re`'s disabled `BinOp` rule carries a TODO about negation and
  implication plus a type-level sketch of an in-progress feature; `Statics.re`'s
  `NOTE(yuchen)` documents a correctness caveat.
- **`Test_Statics_Sums`' `badTypeName`**, reported by an earlier scan — it is
  Hazel source inside a `{|...|}` literal, not OCaml.
- **Seven reported definitions were false positives the build caught.** Each
  became a suppression rule in the detector rather than a one-off exclusion.

## Two things that grew coverage instead of shrinking it

- `Test_Coverage`'s `nested_constructors_exhaustive` and
  `type_function_scrutinee` are complete tests that were never added to the suite
  list. Both pass; now registered (62 -> 64 in that suite).
- `Test_Evaluator_Properties`' `qcheck_preservation_test` was unreferenced
  because its registration was commented out with "Disabled due to known issues
  with preservation". It is now registered as an explicit `Alcotest.skip()` so the
  gap appears in the report instead of hiding as dead code.

## One deletion worth naming

**`VarBstMap`** — a 237-line module plus a 187-line `.rei` — is deleted entirely.
Its only reference in the whole repo was
`module M = { include VarBstMap.Ordered; };` inside a match arm of
`Test_Grammar.re`, where `M` is then never used: a no-op that made the module look
reachable. Flagging it because it is a documented, odoc-commented data structure,
not obviously junk. If anyone wants it kept as future API, this is the commit to
object to.

## Verification

`dune build @src/fmt src --profile release` — the gating CI build, where warnings
32/33/34/37 are errors — is clean. `make test-quick`: **3,268 passing**.

`make dead-code` reports **23** dead definitions in `src/`, not zero:

- **19** are the restorations above, kept at reviewer request.
- **3** arrived dead from the `dev` merge and are not this branch's to judge —
  `CLI/Run.re`'s `evaluate_with_probe_map`, `Refractors.persist`, and
  `Token.of_projector_invoke_opt`, all landed by the fast-parse work and not yet
  wired up.
- **1**, `TutorialGrading.percentage_view`, is removed by #2437's
  `include Grading;` dedup, one branch up the stack.

So the detector-zero claim from round 1 no longer holds, deliberately. Anyone
re-running the sweep should read the table above first.

title: Unskip five sort tests; surface the hidden menhir elaboration test
body:
Two tests that existed but never ran. Net effect is more coverage, not less.

## Five sort tests were skipped waiting on a PR that merged 14 months ago

`Test_Evaluator_Builtins_Lists` skipped five `sort` cases under:

```
// These fail due to an eval bug
// Should work after https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/pull/1729
```

#1729 merged 2025-07-02. All five pass now, so the `Alcotest.skip()` wrappers are
gone and the bodies are back to the same shape as their neighbours.

## `Test_Elaboration` had the suite's only commented-out registration

`"Inconsistent case (menhir)"` was commented out of the `tests` list while its
implementation stayed compiled — so it looked like a live test to anyone reading
the file, and was invisible to anyone reading the results.

Re-enabling it **fails, for a real reason**: menhir wraps each match-branch body
in `Asc(_, Unknown(SynSwitch))` where `MakeTerm` does not, so the two parses are
unequal. That is the same menhir/`MakeTerm` divergence class as the tests already
skipped via `skip_menhir_maketerm_equivalent_test` in `Test_Menhir.re`.

So it is now **registered and explicitly skipped**, with the reason recorded in a
comment next to it, rather than hidden in a commented-out line. It shows up in
the run as a skip instead of silently not existing.

This is a judgement call worth a reviewer's opinion: I chose "visible skip with a
documented reason" over "delete it" or "fix the divergence". Fixing it means
deciding whether menhir or `MakeTerm` is right about that `Asc` wrapper, which is
out of scope for a cleanup branch.

## Also

`Test_ExplainThis.re` had pre-existing formatting drift from the merge-base;
`make dev` auto-promotes it, so it is committed here to stop it showing up as
spurious churn in later branches.

## Verification

Full suite run at the time: **3302 tests, passing.** `make dev` clean.

title: Repo hygiene: stale docs, a dead npm dep, and a dangerous leftover script
body:
Four unrelated small cleanups. None of them touch compiled behaviour.

## Drop `src/util`'s warning-policy override

`src/util/dune` carried the repo's only per-library OCaml flags override — every
other dune file overrides `js_of_ocaml` flags only — with no comment explaining
it:

- `(dev (flags :standard -warn-error -A))` disabled all warnings-as-errors for
  util in the profile `make dev`/`test`/`ci` use.
- `(release (flags :standard -warn-error +A-58))` replaced the workspace's tuned
  release set, dropping `-strict-sequence`, `-strict-formats`, `-short-paths`,
  `-keep-locs` for util.

It was hiding nothing: both profiles are clean with it gone. This is the change
most likely to have been load-bearing, so it is the one worth verifying
independently.

## Delete `scripts/migrate_precedence.{sh,md}`

The migration completed in `054e5df2b9`. Keeping it is **actively dangerous**:
its `needs_migration()` guard matches `(Concave 35|36|37|38|40|43|44|47)`, and
35, 37, 44 and 47 are also *post*-migration values, so all 9 files under
`src/web/init/docs/` still match. Re-running it would silently corrupt every one
of them.

## Drop `@esbuild-plugins/node-resolve`

Nothing imports it: not `prebundle.js`, not `vite.config.mts`, and
`src/web/www/dune` invokes bare `esbuild`. Removing it also drops 10
transitive-only packages and correctly re-marks `esbuild` as dev-only, since it
was a peer dependency of the removed package — hence the lockfile churn.

`@types/node` stays. It looks unreferenced but `vite.config.mts` imports `fs`
and `path`.

## Doc drift

| file | fix |
|---|---|
| `INSTRUCTORS.md` | `make student` / `student-release` → `dev-student` / `release-student` (neither old name is a target) |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | `src/hazelweb/www/` → `src/web/www/` |
| `INSTALL.md` | `Updating.md` → `Updating-OCaml-Version.md` |
| `docs/modules.md` | `statics/Elaborator.re` is gone (elaboration lives in `Statics.re`); `tiles/Arms.re` moved to `web/app/editors/decoration/Arms.re` |

Also removes the `Version_autogenerated.re` gitignore rule — nothing generates or
references that name.

## Verification

`dune build @src/fmt src --profile release` and `make dev` both clean.

title: Swap TutorialSettings for student builds
body:
`setup-instructor` / `setup-student` swapped `ExerciseSettings` but never
`TutorialSettings`, so `TutorialSettings.re` stayed at its committed
`show_instructor = true` in **every** build.

`src/web/app/editors/mode/TutorialsMode.re:437` gates the "Toggle Instructor

tutorial mode.**

The `_instructor` / `_student` variants already existed and hold the values you
would expect — only the `cp` rules in the Makefile were missing:

```
TutorialSettings.re            show_instructor = true    (committed state)
TutorialSettings_instructor.re show_instructor = true
TutorialSettings_student.re    show_instructor = false   (never copied anywhere)
```

## The fix

Two `cp` lines, mirroring the `ExerciseSettings` ones that were already there.

As with `ExerciseSettings.re`, `TutorialSettings.re` is now rewritten by
`make dev` / `make dev-student`, so it will show as modified in a student
checkout. Same pre-existing pattern, one more file.

browser: `make dev-student`, then check that tutorial mode no longer offers the
instructor toggle — I have not run that check, and it is the only thing that
proves the user-visible half.

This is the only user-visible change in the surrounding cleanup work; everything
else there is dead-code removal, tooling, or interfaces. It is based directly on

title: Add an ocaml-index-based dead-code detector
body:
Pure tooling — no source changes, nothing deleted. The deletions in the
follow-on branches are justified by what this reports, so it is worth reading
first even though it is the least interesting diff.

## Why

OCaml's warning 32 is per-compilation-unit. This repo has ~9 `.rei` files
against ~485 `.re`, so essentially every top-level binding is exported and the
compiler cannot see cross-module dead code. **No dune warning setting changes
this** — not dev, and not the strict release profile that CI gates on.

The previous approach was a whole-program text scan. It was wrong twice in ways
the compiler caught (trailing primes, ppx-synthesised call sites) and blind in
ways nothing caught (self-recursive-only functions, members of nested
`module X = {...}`).

## What

`dune` was already building 11 `.ocaml-index` files — the `@ocaml-index` alias
is wired into five Makefile targets and **nothing consumed the output**. Each
library's index records occurrences located in its own files but keyed by the
*defining* uid, so the union of all 11 is complete cross-library reference data.

The predicate: **a uid is dead iff every recorded occurrence lies within the
source span of its own definition.** Self-recursive calls fall inside the span
by construction, which was the text scan's largest blind spot. Runs in ~3s.

`make dead-code`, `dead-code-json`, `dead-code-summary` (markdown, for
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`). If you have run any of
`make dev`/`watch`/`test`/`test-quick`/`watch-test`, the index build is a no-op.

## Reviewing the rules

Every rule in the script exists because it killed an *observed* false positive —
found by deleting what the tool reported and then building. The four in the
third commit each produced a build break or broken code first. The ones most
worth a reviewer's attention:

- **ocaml-index columns are byte offsets, not character offsets.** Decoding
  source as UTF-8 shifted every column past `Node.text("·")` in
  `TextAreaProj.re`.
- **ppx-generated call sites are absent from the index entirely.**
  `RichProbeRegistry.yojson_of_packed_action` has exactly one occurrence — its
  own definition — despite being resolved by a `[@deriving yojson]`. So a
  name-based suppression for deriver conventions is mandatory, not a heuristic.
  It is blunt and will hide a genuinely dead `pp_foo`.
- **Modules with a `.rei` are skipped**, deferring to warning 32, which is right
  where this tool is not.
- `{|...|}` literals break the indentation-based span, and this repo's tests
  embed whole Hazel programs at column 0.

Suppressed candidates are classified and reportable (`--show-suppressed`), not
silently dropped.

## Limits, documented in the script header

Will not catch unused constructors, record fields, types,
`module`/`exception`/`external` bindings, pattern bindings, or mutually
recursive dead groups. Above all it is a **"no recorded reference" tool, not a
reachability analysis** — delete, then build. Do not point it at a
`bisect_ppx`-instrumented build; uid numbering differs.

## Also here

- `.PHONY` was missing six real targets including `ci` — a stray file named `ci`
  would have silently broken the CI build.
- `.gitignore`: `*.log` (two 0-byte scratch logs were sitting untracked at the
  root) and `__pycache__/`/`*.pyc`.

## Verification

`dune build @src/fmt src --profile release` and `make dev` both clean. No source
files are touched, so behaviour is unchanged by construction.

`--baseline`/`--check` (a ratchet mode that fails only on *new* entries) is
implemented but deliberately not wired into CI.

title: PBT all of it
body:
# Full-syntax PBT generators

Our PBTs ran against hand-written generators covering a curated subset of the
language — no modules, no `theorem`/`forall`, no invalid tiles, labeled tuples only
in a few positions. This replaces them with ppx-derived generators that reach **every**
constructor of the Menhir AST, and fixes everything that fell out.

One commit adds the generators, one commit per suite flips it over and fixes what it
finds, one commit deletes the old generators. Each migration commit is self-contained.

Two things that change across the board:

- **`size` changed meaning.** `arb_exp(50)` was a node budget; `arb_exp_full(5)` is
  depth fuel, halved per recursive step. Counts drop 10 000 → 1 000: full-syntax terms
  are far more expensive to build and evaluate. Wider per term, fewer terms.
- **Failures are real.** The generator only emits terms the printer and Menhir lexer
  round-trip, and `Canonicalize` absorbs genuine print aliases, so a failure means a gap.

---

### `Stop ExplicitNonlabel shrinkers from looping forever`

- `shrink_{exp,pat,typ}` returned `ExplicitNonlabel` *for* `ExplicitNonlabel` — a
  shrinker yielding its own input, so QCheck never terminates. Now `Iter.empty`.

### `Add ppx-derived full-syntax QCheck generators`

Derives `arb_exp_full` / `arb_typ_full` from the Menhir AST. Shaping needed to stay
inside what the lexer and printer can express:

- Identifiers, livelit names (`^name`), constructor names get `[@gen]` so they stay
  lexically valid.
- `Invalid*` payloads draw from a closed face-token set (`^o^`, `?_?`, …) — the junk
  tiles MakeTerm actually classifies as `Invalid`. Operator-shaped junk (`!!!`) molds
  as an infix with holes instead, so it's useless as an `Invalid` example.
- Lists capped at 0–3; the ppx default reaches ~10k and explodes recursive terms.
- `TupLabel` left sides restricted to `Label` / `ExplicitNonlabel` — the only forms
  that print and parse as `lab=e` / `_=e`.
- `UnknownType` only generates the printable `EmptyHole`; `Module` binders are
  `VarPat` only; `DynamicErrorHole`'s payload must parse as an error sexp.

Also:

- `ppx_minimal_idents` lets a suite ask for `x`/`y` instead of random letters, so
  generated programs actually bind things.
- Generators are memoized by fuel — building one eagerly expands to
  ~`positions^log2(n)` closures, and rebuilding per suite OOMs Node.
- `Conversion.Typ.of_core_type_provenance` raised on any provenance but
  `Internal`/`EmptyHole`, which crashed shrinking (it goes through `~rev`). Every
  provenance now maps to a printable form.
- Sort-specific renames: `ExplicitNonlabel` → `ExplicitNonlabel{,Pat,Type}`.

### `Migrate Test_Grammar PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- One-liner. Annotation map/unmap was already total.

### `Migrate Test_Elaboration PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- `case (()) | _ => [(let `a` = x in x)] end` — a quoted-label binder synthesizes
  `Label("a")`, which reached `Coverage.all_ctrs_of_type` and hit its
  "non-normalized type" `failwith`. A `Label` isn't a sum; it joins the non-sum forms.
- Bare `_` in pat sort is `ExplicitNonlabel` at the MakeTerm tip, but `PatternMatch`
  only knows `Wild`. Elaboration now emits `Wild` and keeps the mark.

### `Migrate Test_Statics_Properties PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

This suite asserts elaboration is a fixed point, so every fix is about idempotence.

- `x((?))` where `x` is an unknown builtin — dynamics raises `InvalidBuiltin` for
  anything outside `Builtins.forms_init`. Unknown names now elaborate to `Invalid`
  (Indet under `Transition`, same synthesized type). Not `Var`, which would resolve
  against an enclosing binding of the same name.
- `proof_of` quoted the *user* term while `elab_term` held the elaborated one, so
  re-elaboration produced a type that wasn't `fast_equal` to the recorded one — and
  broke the side condition on the `(ProofObject, ProofOf)` ascription rule. Both now
  quote `e_elab`.
- `FixF` wrapped its body in `Asc` unconditionally, adding a layer per pass. Now only
  when the ascription would change the body's type.
- Constructor patterns recomputed `elab_ty` even when already resolved, regressing it
  to `Some(None)` on the second pass.
- Test side: the elaborated program must be re-checked with `use_mode = None`.
  `use SInt in -?` elaborates to an `SInt` minus, which a `Some(Int)` pass rewrites
  back to `Int`. (`CachedStatics` already does this.)

### `Migrate Test_Evaluator_Properties PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

- `let y = y in y` → substitution produced `let y' = y' in y'`. The RHS isn't under
  the binder, so freshening a shadowing binder must not rewrite it.
- `fun x -> 1` with a `Sig` in the annotation slot — only *surface* ascriptions go
  through `desugar_sig`, so substitution met a `SigLet` pattern inside a type and hit
  a `failwith`. Signature names are field labels, not expression binders, so we
  recurse and leave them alone; statics also normalizes `Fun`'s annotation now.
- `fix x -> (theorem ? = y in x)` — `Theorem`/`Forall` step to Indet but their bodies
  still mention environment variables. Without `wrap_closure`, big-step left `x` free
  while small-step substituted.
- `forall x(x) -> x` — big-step alpha-renames the later binder, small-step doesn't.
  `Alphas.combine` is first-match, so duplicate binders need the *later* binders
  passed first to shadow correctly.
- `DynamicErrorHole((()))` — the `req_final` binder shadowed the outer term, so
  `wrap_closure` wrapped the child and dropped the hole.

### `Migrate Test_TextRoundtrip PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- One-liner. The print→parse→print fixed point already held.

### `Migrate Test_Menhir PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

The big one — Menhir↔MakeTerm equivalence is what full syntax exposes most.

**Menhir learns the syntax it was missing:** `theorem`, `forall`, `proof_object`,
`proof_of`, `Nat`/`SInt`, quoted labels in pat and typ position, invalid faces in every
sort, `module _ =` / `module ? =`, `hint <exp> test … end` (was string-literal only),
and `undef` → `undefined`.

Two restructurings:

- **`sumTerm` derives `typ`.** MakeTerm classifies *any* type in sum position —
  `TypVar` → `Variant`, else `BadEntry` — so `sumTerm` does too. Because it can then
  derive a leading-plus sum, `+ A + B` reduced to `Sum([BadEntry(Sum …)])` where
  MakeTerm has a flat sum; `splice_sumterm` flattens it back.
  Heads of *no-lead* sums (`Nil + Cons(Int, T)`, `HasInt(Int) + HasMore(...)`) get
  their own nonterminal, since an applied constructor isn't a `typ` and a general
  `sumTerm PLUS …` head would be swallowed by the leading-plus rules.
- **`typ` split into `typ`/`typ_inner`** so `...` sits looser than `->`, matching
  `Precedence`. `%prec` can't express it — `TUPLE_EXTENSION` also carries exp-level
  precedence. Function params gain a layer so ascription binds tighter than cons:
  `fun p : T :: q ->` is `ConsPat(AscPat(p,T), q)`, as MakeTerm reads it.

**Where the two parsers disagreed:**

- `undefined . ((`l`))` — Menhir erases parens, so the `.` field tip has to peel them
  or MakeTerm sees a field access and Menhir a `MultiHole`. Same for `=` tips.
- `{ o^o }` — MakeTerm collapsed a leaf `Invalid` in mod position to a hole, which
  erases the token entirely.
- `^w^ -> Int` — an invalid face is an *Exp*-sorted tile, so it drags the whole type
  out of Typ sort and the arrow vanishes. `(^w^) -> Int` agrees. Precedence can't fix
  this: an invalid hole is atomic, so it never trips the paren check.
- `?:+^w^` — same trap, but a sum has no single protectable operand; the ascription
  itself is lost. So a sum containing an invalid gets parenthesized whole.
- `hint _ test _ end` with a nested `test … end` — during LTR insert, `test` matched
  deep in the backpack and completed `HintedTest`'s own shard instead of expanding a
  nested `Test`. Leading expanders now only match at the top of the stack (as
  ambiguous polymorphs already did), and hints are force-parenthesized.
- `|=>` inside `{}` — `remold` skipped complete kids when parent sorts matched,
  leaving a stale mold whose empty `in_` then broke MakeTerm.
- `(A ... B) ... C`, `T . A -> B` — the parsers order `.`, `->` and `...` differently;
  the printer now parenthesizes defensively on both sides.
- `Invalid(s)` was rewritten to the fixed string `"Invalid"` on the way back to the
  Menhir AST. That runs during shrinking, so shrinking silently turned counterexamples
  into *different programs* — and `"Invalid"` lexes as a constructor, not a face.
- Bare `lab=e` only parses inside `(…)`, so it wraps at binders and at the root while
  tuple fields don't become `((a=1), (b=2))`.
- Module bodies were an unimplemented TODO in the parenthesizer; item payloads are now
  parenthesized and item expressions wrapped so a printed `;` stays a separator.

**`test/Canonicalize.re`** is the new normalizer: it rewrites a generated term into the
shape print+parse produces (`BuiltinFun` → `Var`, `Nat`/`SInt` → `Int`, floats via
their printed form, `DynamicErrorHole` stripped, bare `TupLabel` → singleton tuple,
`f(_)` → `DeferredAp`). Round-trip and cross-parser tests canonicalize both sides and
then compare *strictly*, instead of loosening the equality relation — one place to look
when a print alias shows up, and `Equality` stays honest.

### `Migrate Test_MenhirFuzz PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- Same switch, and it drops its own bespoke equality settings for `Canonicalize`.

### `Migrate Test_ExplainThis PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- No production fix needed — `decide` handled everything. Adds a regression test
  walking every info-map entry of `let 0 = _ in []` and `fun 0 -> []`.

### `Remove the curated AST generators`

- Deletes ~580 lines of hand-written generators and their wrappers.

---

Side effect worth noting: menhir's arbitrarily resolved reduce/reduce conflicts drop
from **52 on `dev` to 5**, and it no longer reports any never-reduced productions
(`dev` has 3). Shift/reduce goes 57 → 69.

title: Agent hardening: eval-settled probes, storage rework, member-path tools
body:
These are several agent fixes/enhancements which came up in trials generating user-defined livelits with the agent. 

- The biggest one was decreasing parse time for large code insertions, enabled by #2426 which this is stacked on.
- Better agent probing: Previously the agent probe action did not wait for the worker to return, requiring a multi-round potentially race-conditiony process to actually see probed values. Now waits before sending results to model; checks in 150ms beats until the eval result settles (bounded ~10s). 
- Chat storage is reworked around per-chat records (a fresh agent's persisted state drops from ~152KB to ~2KB); these could get quite large and effect agent latency
- The edit tools plus view/probe tools address module members through owner/member paths
- funlet fix supporting `let f(x) = e` paths for modules
- Stubbed read_docs doc-pack registry which will be populated in user-livelits; this enables breaking up the system prompt into on-demand docs files


---
### Fixes brought over from the aria-demo branch (2026-09-09)
Six independent one-commit fixes, ~105 lines total. Each was verified to be a dev-level problem before landing here (details in the commit messages).
- d398436869 Menhir: `Int(x)`-style patterns (type-keyword constructors) no longer fall back to the slow parser.
- c704c8149f + 84fd46f42c Worker: the reuse pre-pass ran twice per request and every node paid a reuse check; now once, and only above 2500 statics entries. Drag-to-result on a ~100-line program went 2.0 s → 0.2 s.
- 0953ad542b Projector commits (slider, checkbox, livelit gestures) skip the 225 ms typing debounce.
- 6c1d1a930d Probe All: ambient samples capture no environment (was ~80% of retained heap; worker 1.8 GB → 186 MB on a 150-line program).
- 8afaf6dfd4 Follow-up to the above, easy to drop: placing a probe under Probe All re-evaluates so the new probe's context menu still shows bindings.

title: Fast parsing for complete terms
body:
This introduces a fast path to all editor parse paths which attempts to use the Menhir parser, falling back to the per-character editor parser if it does not succeed. The new fast path lexes the source into tokens + whitespace gaps, parses with Menhir, print the term back to a segment via ExpToSegment, then weaves the original tokens and whitespace back in positionally. This is done so that we have string fidelity by construction (doesn't reply on completion provenance to e.g. preserve float rep), but more importantly so that MakeTerm's someone-edge-casey whitespace-attachment policy stays single-homed. A fall back to the slow path prints a `SLOW PARSE (context, N chars)` console line naming the caller. Parser agreement is pinned by differential suites (QCheck equivalence property, fuzz, per-file corpus term diff, and an empty-known-gaps ratchet that every `.hz` in the repo must fast-parse).

This involved making a bunch of patches and extensions to the menhir parser.

All docs slides, and basically all serialized hazel programs, are now just .hz text files. Exceptions include the in-built derivations (neither Claude nor I was inclined to touch this) and exercises mode (as it would remove our security by obscurity). All of these are parsed on-demand now, which makes editor startup time less than a second. Each current doc slides parses in less than 50ms.

The previous backup_text tests are replaced by tests that do both parse paths for each slide to see if they match up, which should force keeping both in sync as long as we add new syntax to the slides

Also:
- `Equality.pat_names_equal` reflexivity fix: identical literal module-let patterns (`let [] = ...`) compared unequal (found by the equivalence property).
- Persistence: backup text prints holes as `¿` (lossless), unpersist is fast-first, sexp fallback retired; b2t2 Datasheet now a a `^^text` slide.
- CLI parses fast-first and no longer loads the slide set holistically on invocation.

title: Simplify ExplainThis: forms own their colorings, one id enum, total model
body:
## What this does

`ExplainThis.get_doc` was a ~3100-line match in which every branch re-derived by hand which form of a doc group to show and which sub-terms it should highlight. The data a form needs was scattered: its explanation was a `%s` template in `data/`, filled by `Scanf.format_from_string` in `ExplainThis.re`; its colorings were a function in `data/` invoked at the call site; its specificity level was recomputed by comparing an explicitly named form id against the group's first form.

This branch moves all of it onto the form itself and deletes the scaffolding that existed to carry it around.

This is the direction issue #1170 asks for — generalize the `Simple` infrastructure so it isn't limited to singleton groups — reached by making the invariant enforceable rather than by rewriting all 154 forms.

| | dev | this branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| `ExplainThis.re` | 3117 | 1753 (−44%) |
| `ExplainThisForm.re` | 513 | 390 |
| `ExplainThisModel.re` | 225 | 174 |
| `format_from_string` sites | 95 | 0 |
| `get_specificity_level` references | 47 | 3 |
| `~colorings` arguments at call sites | 44 | 4 |
| id enums to keep in sync | 2 × 111 | 1 |
| raises in `ExplainThisModel` | 6 | 0 |
| test-only constructs in production types | — | 0 |

## How it's staged

Commits are written to be read in order; each says what it changes and what it deliberately leaves alone.

**Stage 0 — pin the behavior first.** `get_doc` gains a `Probe` mode that reports the decision it makes and renders nothing, so the golden can be written before anything moves. The color map could not serve as the fingerprint: it is re-derived from the explanation's markdown links and never reads `colorings` at all, so it is blind to the mapping under change. The golden canonicalizes each UUID to the printed text of the sub-term it belongs to, and sweeps every form of every group (by planting a selection), since `init` otherwise only ever reaches the most specific form. *(`Probe` is scaffolding and is deleted again in Stage 4 — see below.)*

**Stage 1 — remove the scaffolding.** Explanations are filled at their definition site so the compiler checks arity; the 44 specificity ladders collapse into one `leveled(~fallback, group)` helper; `group_id` becomes an alias of `form_id` (the two listed the *same 111 constructors*), which makes a `singleton` combinator expressible — 86 single-form groups now derive their id from their form.

**Stage 2 — colorings onto forms.** `form` gains a `colorings` field, filled per module. That the form-carried mapping really matches what the call sites were passing was established by temporarily inverting the precedence and rerunning the golden; exactly four cases differed, all fallback rows, all preserved deliberately.

**Stage 3 — totality and a wasted pass.** `ExplainThisModel` becomes raise-free, and `Page.re` stops computing a full `get_doc` pass it then discards.

**Stage 4 — split the decision from the rendering, and remove the seam.** `message_mode` was a tag telling one function which of three unrelated things to return — Vdom, a color map, or (Stage 0's addition) a test callback. `get_doc` becomes `decide`, returning a `decision` (`NoDoc` / `Prose` / `Markdown` / `DrvSyntax` / `Doc {group, form, options, explanation, colorings}`); `view_doc` and `color_map_of` are then ordinary functions over it. `message_mode`, the `probe` record and its test-only `sf_ids` field are gone, and the test calls `decide` directly. It's a small diff because the ~150 dispatch arms were already tail calls and are textually unchanged.

## User-visible changes

- **Type-function abstract form is now highlighted.** `get_doc` handed the `TypFunctionExp` group *`FunctionExp`'s* coloring function, so the `typfun a -> e` abstract in the sidebar was never coloured and hovering its links highlighted nothing. This is the concrete failure that motivated moving colorings onto the form. Verified in the browser.
- **Collapsing the sidebar no longer disables code highlighting.** `get_color_map_deduction` guarded on `settings.explainThis.show` while `get_color_map` used `settings.sidebar.show`; nothing toggles the former and it defaults to true, so collapsing the sidebar stopped highlighting for ordinary terms but not derivation ones. Both now read `sidebar.show`.
- **Two forms' persisted feedback keys move.** `AppPat.funapp_pat` claimed `ApConsPat` in group `ApFuncPat`; `TerminalPat.sintlit_pat` claimed `IntPat` in group `SIntPat`. Neither is reachable through the UI (both groups are singletons, so no expander renders), but a user who had rated either keeps an orphaned row that now reads as unrated.
- **Prose typos fixed**: "raising left ro the right", "This if functionally equivalent", "evalutes", "autmatically" (×2).
- **One less full `get_doc` pass per frame** when the cursor is in a derivation cell.

## Bugs fixed along the way

- Two `%s`/`%d` mismatches (`FunctionExp.function_sintlit_exp`, `LetExp.let_sint_exp`) that were guaranteed `Scan_failure` if reached — surfaced by making the formats compile-checked.
- `ExplainThisModel.get_options` raised for any form in a multi-form group lacking an `expandable_id`, and 47 of 154 forms have none — so adding a form to a two-form group would have crashed the sidebar. The invariant held by luck, not construction.
- Several dead branches that passed a mismatched group (`Prod([])` → `TupleTyp.tuple2`, the 0-tuple type case).

## Testing

- `make dev` clean and warning-free on a forced rebuild.
- `make test-quick`: 3255 tests pass.
- 35 characterization cases plus two structural assertions, in `test/Test_ExplainThis.re`:
  - the set of group ids the corpus reaches is asserted *exactly*, with a separate `known_unreachable` list asserted **not** reached, so losing coverage fails loudly instead of going quiet;
  - every coloring's piece id must occur in its own form's `syntactic_form` — naming a piece the form doesn't contain is always a bug and a silent one, since the pair simply never matches and the link renders unhighlighted.
- Zero golden diff at every refactoring step; the deliberate diffs are one line for the `ApFuncPat` fix and the coverage additions.

The corpus is hand-written because `AST.gen_exp_sized` cannot produce `Asc`, `Use`, `SInt`/`Nat`, module forms or pipelines, so the property test cannot reach those docs at all.

## Review notes

- **Locally-created pieces** (`cons`, `comma`, `ap`, Grout holes) were hoisted to module level, because forms are now rebuilt per call and `Piece.id`s must stay stable. This is the change with the most plausible visual failure mode.
- **Four `~colorings` overrides remain and are load-bearing**: `FunctionExp.function_exp`, `LetExp.let_base_exp`, `LetExp.let_tuple_exp`, `ListPat.cons_base_pat`. A least-specific form is shared across a whole family (one `function_exp` backs all 19 `FunctionExp` groups), so it is not built for any one call site. This is also why `FunctionExp(Base)` and `LetExp(Base)` never appear as a *group*.
- **`Fun`'s fallback links a different id than its specific forms**: for `fun (x) -> x` the `Base` form highlights `(x)` and `Var` highlights `x`. Preserved as-is with a comment rather than silently changed — each highlight matches the wording of the form doing the describing, but it's worth a deliberate decision.
- **Unused id constructors are kept on purpose** (`TrivExp` and others). They appear in persisted `ExplainThisModel` state, and removing a variant makes `t_of_sexp` fail on a stored model that names it. For the same reason `settings.explainThis.show` is left in place though now unread.
- **The 53 `*_id: form_id` constants in `data/`** existed to feed the specificity comparisons and now only label their own form. Left rather than inlined, since restating a `form_id` by hand is the same class of mistake as the two id mismatches fixed here.

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- The dispatch still runs twice per frame — once in `calculate` for the code highlights, once in `view` for the sidebar. `decide` now returns a plain value that *could* be computed once, but the two callers sit on opposite sides of the calculate/view boundary **and do not pass the same input**: `ExplainThis.view` applies `Info.pre_labeled_info` to the cursor info while `Page.re`'s `get_color_map` call does not. Sharing one decision between them is therefore a behavior change rather than a pure optimization, and that asymmetry deserves its own look — it may well be a bug.
- `SIntPat` docs appear unreachable from the editor: `MakeTerm` only ever builds `Atom(Int)` literal patterns from surface syntax. Asserted unreachable rather than fixed.
- The `SInt`/`Nat` binary operators are admitted by `Operators.op_bin` and `form_id` but `OpExp` defines no docs for them, so they fall through to "No docs available". Also asserted, not fixed.
- The golden records which *user-code* ids a doc links, not which *abstract-form piece* each is paired with. That's why the TypFun bug needed a browser check — the new piece-membership assertion now covers that class going forward.

## Stacking

The first commit (`ExplainThis: fill doc explanations at definition, drop runtime formats`) is the tip of `explainthis-compile-checked-docs`, which has no PR of its own. It is included here. `ExplainThis PBT` also appears in history; the equivalent landed on dev separately as #2414, and the merge takes dev's reviewed version.

title: Cost display: billed cost, cached tokens, and cache savings
body:
## What

Two related pieces:

### 1. Cost display: billed cost, cached tokens, and cache savings

Surfaces the caching/cost data dev already records (per-request OpenRouter `cost`, cache read/write tokens) in the UI:

- **`/cost`** now shows **Billed** (actual OpenRouter charge), **cached tokens**, and **Saved** (list price − billed), alongside the existing list-price estimate.
- **Per-message expanded usage rows**: "Cached this turn", "Saved by caching", and the exact per-token input price used — numbers are auditable, not trust-us.
- **Fixes input-token inflation**: OpenRouter folds the cache write into `prompt_tokens` on cache-write turns, so raw sums read ~2× high. Session totals and the per-message meter now subtract `cache_write_tokens`.

### 2. Prompt-caching eval suite (`agent-docs/caching-eval/`)

- **`./hazel agent-eval`** (new CLI subcommand): drives the **real `Agent.Update` loop headless** against live OpenRouter — real system prompt + dev notes cache anchor, real tools/tool execution, real payload serialization and usage parsing — via a synchronous curl-backed XHR polyfill in `src/CLI/polyfill.js`. Simulates a user session with scripted inputs.
- **`harness/run_eval.mjs`**: provider-isolated JS control harness (byte-mirrors the wire shape, no app code) with a free `--dry-run` cost estimator.
- Append-only JSONL data accumulators (raw requests/responses, per-turn results, verdicts, `/credits` ledger) + pre-implementation report + findings.

### Findings from the full 4-model run (2026-08-04)

| model | caching | note |
|---|---|---|
| claude-haiku-4.5 | ✅ working | turn-2 cost −87% |
| claude-sonnet-4.6 | ✅ working | session saved $1.16 vs list |
| gemini-3-flash-preview | ✅ working | confirms the `prompt_tokens` double-report this PR corrects |
| qwen/qwen3-coder | ❌ **not caching at all** | billed ~4× Haiku for an equivalent session |

The eval also exercised this PR's `cost_payload` accumulator live — billed/cached/saved came out coherent, and the "saved" line correctly vanishes where nothing was saved.

## Testing

- Full suite passes (3296 tests), clean build (including the new CLI target).
- Live validation: real headless agent sessions across 4 models (data committed under `agent-docs/caching-eval/outputs/`), `/cost` cross-checked against raw provider usage.

title: ci: fix Actions cache eviction, split into independent jobs, enforce release warnings on test/
body:
Part of the CI/CD plan on #2203. Closes #2456.

## What changed

- **Replaced the one serial job with three independent ones.** `Build and Deploy Hazel` was a
  single 21–31.5 min job that published the preview and *then* ran the tests — one check covering
  everything, with the test result buried after a deploy that had already happened. Now
  `Fast checks`, `Full tests` and `Deploy branch preview` are three jobs with no `needs:` between
  them. Each re-runs alone, so a flaky suite costs one job rather than another deploy and another
  30 minutes, and the fast signal comes back in ~4 minutes instead of at the end of the full run.

- **Turned off `setup-ocaml`'s dune cache and made the opam switch cache single-writer.** Its
  entries are keyed on the run id, so they never hit, and 10.24 GiB of them were evicting the
  `_opam` switch from a 10 GiB budget. The switch cache is now `restore` + `save` with
  `dev`/`bot-update-deps` as the only writers, plus `restore-keys` for a warm start after a
  lockfile bump.

  Caching the switch ourselves is deliberate and unsupported: `setup-ocaml` declines to do it
  (ocaml/setup-ocaml#1098), on the grounds that cached dependencies drift from opam-repository.
  We take that trade knowingly — it moves `Install dependencies` from 3–7.5 min to ~6 s, which is
  what sets how long we wait for a deploy and for static-check feedback — and the lock file bounds
  the risk. It doesn't eliminate it: in-place edits to already-published packages have broken us
  before (#2334).
- **Added `make ci-check` to enforce release warnings on `test/`** (#2456). `dune build @check
  --profile release` type-checks both trees without linking — 21 s, no second build of the test
  bundle. Warnings in `test/` previously printed and passed.
- **Made test failures produce a non-zero exit code.** Alcotest is run with `and_exit:false` so
  the JUnit report can be written first, and junit_alcotest hands the outcome back as a function
  to call afterwards — the only thing that propagates a failure. `test/haz3ltest.re` discarded
  it, so the test binary exited 0 whatever happened, and every entry point keyed on that exit
  code passed on a red suite: `dune runtest`, `make ci`, `make test`, `make test-quick` and
  `./run_tests`.
- **Published the test reports as check runs** (`use-actions-summary: false`). The default writes
  results to the run's job summary and creates no check run, so `Test Report` never appeared in a
  PR's check list — nothing to click through to, no inline annotations on failing tests, and
  nothing that could be named as a required status on `dev`.

## What runs where

```
checks.yml   ── on: workflow_call                       the definitions, one copy
   ├── Fast checks       fmt → make ci-check → make ci-quick → Quick Test Report
   └── Full tests        make ci → Test Report → Codecov

ci.yml       ── on: push, except gh-readonly-queue/** | merge_group
   └── calls checks.yml

fork-ci.yml  ── on: pull_request, if the pull request comes from a fork
   └── calls checks.yml, with the report and coverage steps off

deploy.yml   ── on: push, except gh-readonly-queue/**
   └── Deploy branch preview    release build → hazel.org/build/<branch>
```

Every filter is a trigger rather than an `if:`, which leaves **two conditionals in the whole
system**: the fork test, and one input that turns off the report check runs and the Codecov
upload for forks, whose `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only and which get no secrets.

**`ci.yml` has no `pull_request` trigger on purpose.** A same-repo pull request fires both it and
`push` for the same commit, so the full suite would run twice. Forks are the only case `push`
cannot see — a fork's pushes happen in the fork — and `fork-ci.yml` covers them.

**Fork PRs gain CI.** Today's `deploy_branches.yml` is `on: [push]`, so fork PRs get no checks at
all; 3 of the last 200 PRs here came from forks. They now get `Fast checks` and `Full tests`,
without the report check runs their token can't create. They still get no branch preview.

**No merge queue exists yet**, but both `ci.yml` triggers are load-bearing once one does. A queue
pushes its `gh-readonly-queue/**` branch, yet Actions only reports status into the queue from a
`merge_group` run — so the trigger is what makes the queue's checks exist, and `branches-ignore`
is what stops the same commit being checked twice and a speculative merge being published as a
preview. Turning the queue on is #2203 phase 4.

**Why formatting, warnings and the quick suite share a job.** Every job installs OCaml and the
dependencies independently, ~2 min warm and 5–9 min cold, which is more than those three checks
cost to run. Splitting them would buy precise names and precise retry for roughly double the
wall clock. Worth revisiting after the build-once artifact work in the follow-ups, which is what
makes extra jobs cheap.

`Build release` is no longer a separate gate — the deploy job runs the same command. That leaves
`src/web`'s `main` and `worker` jsoo executables unlinked on fork PRs and in the merge queue,
which we're accepting until it causes a problem; `Full tests` still links the `web` library
through the test bundle.

## Notes for merge

- **`make test` and `./run_tests` now fail on a red suite.** That's the point, but it may surface
  failures that have been passing silently across the open PRs — #2128's evaluator/stepper QCheck
  flake most likely.
- The strict formatting gate wasn't in the original plan and can turn other branches red. Easy to
  drop.
- **The warm-cache win can't be demonstrated until this reaches `dev`.** Only `dev` and
  `bot-update-deps` write the switch cache, so the first push after merging populates
  `Linux-opam-*` and the *second* is where `Install dependencies` should fall to single digits.
- **Branch protection and the merge queue are both future work** (#2203 phase 4). When you set
  them up, the required checks are named `CI / checks / Fast checks` and `CI / checks / Full
  tests` — the reusable-workflow nesting makes those non-obvious, so it's noted in `ci.yml` too.
  The `merge_group` path is the one thing here that can't be exercised until a queue exists.
- ~~Also pins the opam repository, resolving #2334.~~ Reverted in bd8c01b3b2 — a separate concern
  that made this harder to review. #2334 stays open and gets its own PR.
