title: New decorations architecture
body:
Refactor `UHCode` rendering such that decorations (e.g. err holes, var use, current term indicator) are separate elements laid on top of code text elements. The motivation for this refactor is twofold:
- First, separating decorations from code text allows `Doc`/`Layout` specification to concern itself solely with the static code text, independent of the cursor location and other transient decorations. This minimizes pretty printing recalculation, the primary bottleneck in our view pipeline. (Note: Although docs/layouts no longer carry decoration information in their annotations, we must still regenerate docs whenever there is a change in an err hole or var err hole status, since these are embedded in `UH[Exp|Pat]` and thus affect pointer equality.)
- Second, specifying decorations as independent layers improves modularity and makes it easier to add new decorations in the future. In particular, decorations no longer need to hack z-indices, which caused issues with ongoing work on Hazel assistant.

New pipeline:
```
Structure -> Doc -> Layout -> Box -> Vdom (code text)
                      |
                       --> MeasuredLayout -> Vdom (code decorations)
```

`Box` decomposes a `Layout` into boxes that can be easily translated to HTML structure. In the process of converting an annotated `Layout` node into a `Box` node, the annotated subject may be split into up to three boxes (head, body, tail) with the annotation distributed over the constituents. (It's possible go directly from `Layout` to `Vdom` by opting to lay out all code text in inline format, but that would require inserting additional indentation and annotations would then span those indentation nodes, which isn't true of the original `Doc`/`Layout` structure. Such an approach is simpler to implement and wouldn't cause any issues in the current implementation, but could perhaps cause issues in future use cases. That said, I suspect the `Box` abstraction crept in due to prior concerns when decorations weren't separated from the code text. Open to dropping it. I may also be forgetting other concerns, maybe @adamsmd could chime in here.)

`MeasuredLayout` is the same as `Layout` but adorns each `Layout` node with measurement information. These are used to determine the coordinates of SVG paths for code decorations, which are placed below / on top of the code text. In more detail: `Program.re` provides paths to each decoration in the current program; `UHCode.re` uses those paths to traverse the program's `MeasuredLayout` and identify the terms that need to be decorated; `UHDecoration.re` takes the dimensions of the identified terms and specifies the shape of each decoration as a collection of rectangles, the contour of the union of which forms the decoration shape. The algorithm used to compute this contour is taken from Computational Geometry: An Introduction by Preparata & Shamos, Sections 1.2.3.1, 8.3, 8.5.

`MeasuredLayout` takes over the role of `CursorMap`. On each click/arrow key movement, the dimensions of the `MeasuredLayout` nodes are used to traverse the document in search of `Step` and `Token` annotations in order to determine the next `CursorPath`.

Removed much of `style.css` that was previously devoted to hacking together current term indicator decorations directly embedded in the code text.

title: Fix #356 right sidebar goes off-screen when window isn't wide enough
body:
There's a lot going on with this issue. The first was the code editor
was forced to be a fixed 80ch width which caused a lot of layout problems,
this was removed. The body was changed from flex to grid because that
behaves a bit better in this scenario. The code window was given a min-width
(which is arbitrary can be debated what a better size would be) and the body
was given overflow-x. With overflow-x on the body the side panes behave a bit
better now because if they would force the code area to be too small they push
out the page width instead and add a scroll bar. Overall the layout of the
application should behave a bit better, but there might still be some edge
cases. There were a couple scenarios where overflow wasn't specified and so
the page started vibrating (caught in a layout loop).

Tested with Firefox + Chromium on Linux

title: list literals
body: List Literals are an integral part of any programming language. It's a particularly interesting problem in Hazel, given it's hole-driven programming paradigm. This project involved creating a new UHExp constructor called listlit, which would also end up replacing the already existing constructor listnil. This was done by having listlit take an opseq option type argument, which could then take None as an argument, thus simulating listnil. I also added a new constructor ListLitZ, which handles the zipper cases pertaining to list literals. Most of its logic followed that of ParenthesizedZ, which handles the zipper case corresponding to Parenthesized. Here are some examples: - Creating an empty list. - Constructing a list with single element. - Adding multiple elements to the list. - Creating an empty hole in the middle of the list. - Constructing a list within a list. - Deleting the nested list, which then makes the nested elements belong to the outer list. - Deleting the list, thus making the elements just a sequence of numbers.

title: resetting hole numbering when the expression is complete
body:
In Hazel right now, hole numbers increase monotonically but the numbering is never reset, even when you pass through edit states where there are no holes. This pull request checks if expressions are complete and also renumbers holes. 

The completeness of expression is checked (according to POPL 17 paper) by making sure there are no holes (empty/non-empty/type). For this, I have written is_complete functions in UHPat, UHExp, UHTyp, and OpSeq files. For the purpose of renumbering holes, however, type holes are allowed in expressions. So I have passed a check_type_holes flag to the is_complete functions. This flag is set to false when renumbering holes. Every time there is an edit action in the program, the expression is checked. If there are no empty/non-empty holes (note that type holes are allowed since the check_type_holes flag is set to false), the hole number is reset to 1 (by setting u_gen to MetaVarGen.init). Only empty holes are renumbered.

Testing: Created and deleted holes for different types of expressions and made sure the renumbering of holes happened when required.

title: new year, new codebase
body:
- Refactor core uhnode datatypes so that opseqs may consist of a single element. This removes large volumes of code devoted to handling the prior restriction that opseqs always carry two or more elements. Opseqs are now distinguished types in each uhnode datatype.
- Reorganize modules that traverse uhnode and znode datatype structures into submodules `Typ`, `Pat`, `Exp`. Now, instead of calling `CursorInfo.syn_cursor_info_pat` or `CursorInfo.syn_cursor_info_exp`, you call `CursorInfo.Pat.syn_cursor_info` or `CursorInfo.Exp.syn_cursor_info`.
- We never had proper n-tuples (sometimes there was the illusion of n-tuples working due to other confounding bugs). Modifies `Statics` and `CursorInfo` to support n-tuples.
- Introduce new intermediate `Action` result datatypes that simplify how we handle keywords like `let` and `case`.
- Implement character-level actions and remove all the cruft accumulated in `Cell.re`.
- Rebuild view layer of code on @adamsmd's new pretty printer. See `Doc.re`, `Layout.re`, `LayoutOfDoc.re` for general pretty printing logic. See `TermTag.re`, `TermDoc.re`, and `TermLayout.re` for logic specific to pretty printing Hazel terms. See `Code.re` to see how a `TermLayout.t` gets turned into vdom nodes. Note that `TermLayout` has various decoration functions that get invoked after a `TermDoc.t` gets turned into a `TermLayout.re` (which made it easy to merge @VictorYYW's variable usage decorations).
- Rebuild view layer of code into a separate presentation layer and contenteditable layer. The presentation layer is what the user sees, simulating the blinking caret and showing nice visuals. The actual caret is in the invisible contenteditable element (fixed position outside of viewport) that allows us to hook into existing implementation of text carets. To keep them in sync, we translate caret movements in the contenteditable layer into changes in presentation layer, and we translate clicks on the presentation layer into caret resets in the contenteditable layer. The reason for this approach (which is also taken by VSCode) is that the contenteditable feature limits how we can layout the elements, which makes it hard to style them effectively, so a separate presentation layer frees the implementation of visual styling.
- Introduce distinction between an _open child_ and a _closed child_ of an AST node. An open child is a child that has the same term family (e.g. Typ, Pat, Exp) as the parent -- a closed child is a child with a different term family. A closed child will appear in the UI enclosed in the parent, an open child will have a border but otherwise be unenclosed. This distinction only appears when generating a view of the program, i.e., by the time we have a `TermDoc.t`.
- Introduce new blocks-like UI in which it appears a block representing the current term raises out of the surface to the code text floating above. Use different colors for different term families.

title: Cursor on delimiters + incr_dom + cursor indicators + node staging + cardstacks
body:
This is a massive pull request containing many changes over the past several months. Most notable changes include:
- updating our cursor model so that the caret can be on node delimiters
- restructuring our term datatypes such that each variant has its own err_status field, such that certain variants that don't require it (e.g. EmptyHole, OpSeqs) no longer carry it
- refactor our view layer to use incr_dom
- somewhat simplify pretty printing logic
- enrich our cursor indicators to include current node + current term
- implement first version of node staging
- implements a basic cardstack system for running through exercises in sequence

There are still some fundamental warts to resolve. Some issues are remaining bugs, especially in node staging. The more fundamental issue is that contenteditable, cursor indicators, and incr_dom do not play nicely together in the current implementation. contenteditable requires code to be rendered in dom via inline elements. This means that the shapes we want to overlay with cursor indicators cannot be identified structurally. Instead we must wait until the dom gets rendered on each animation frame by incr_dom, then we take the viewport coordinates of the nodes we want to be overlaid and paint over them. This is also true for nonempty holes. Already we are running into performance issues repainting the cursor indicators and err holes on small programs on each animation frame.

In my next set of changes, I will be addressing these issues by taking an approach similar to VSCode: they create the illusion of text editing by rendering their code in a noneditable structured form (thereby freeing it from the constraints of contenteditable) while using an invisible textarea element to hook into its caret movement+selection logic. Essentially this separate the concerns of editing+movement from the presentation. This will greatly simplify our pretty printing logic and remove the need to paint overlays over our code view on each animation frame.

For now, however, we have been moving forward assuming approximately the current implementation approach, so I'm gonna go ahead and merge these changes so that we can start working off of dev again.

title: Cursor on delimiters
body:
- Modifies our cursor model to support cursors on syntactic delimiters and infix operators. When the cursor is on a delimiter, the owner node of the delimiter is highlighted as the selected expression; when the cursor is on an operator, the operator subsequence whose root is that operator is highlighted.
- Introduces a `CursorEscape` mechanism by which pressing Backspace at the beginning of a node pops the cursor out to the preceding cursor position (e.g., the end of a preceding delimiter); pressing Delete at end of a node has similar behavior.
- Otherwise, if not `CursorEscape`, deleting a delimiter deletes the owner of the delimiter (including all its children). One exception is when there is only a single child node of the same type as the parent node, in which case deleting a parent delimiter unwraps the parent node and leaves the child node in place.
- Implements `do_transport` cases for delimiters, such that the cursor can only be at the start and end of delimiters.
- Adds cursor on case rule delimiters such that the cursor on `|` or `=>` highlights the rule and applies the deletion rules described above to the rule node.

title: Blocks
body:
Refactor line items into blocks. The top level expression form is now a block, which consists of a list of lines and a concluding expression. This refactoring better organizes existing code written to handle line items by separating functionality concerning lines from functionality concerning expressions, particularly in `Action`. By collecting lines in a block into a single top-level list, this refactoring also makes significant progress toward cells, which may contain only lines and no concluding expression -- for example, all cell-level edit actions are already implemented by `Action.syn_perform_lines`.

I started implementing blocks such that there could be block-level hole membranes and block-level cursors. My thinking was that fixing a type error in a block's concluding expression may require fixing something in the preceding lines, so we should expand the hole membrane to include the entire block. I could also see block level-cursors being useful in the future -- it would be interesting to see how we could incorporate ideas from [Greenfoot's frame-based editing](https://www.greenfoot.org/frames/). However, there isn't a good way with our current implementation that lets the user get to a block-level cursor. Maybe this is a case where multiple physical cursor locations would be useful. In any case, this would require more thought and additional substantial work. For now, there is no hole membrane or cursor position at the block level.

title: Keywords
body:
Makes `let` and `case` reserved keywords. Variables in both pattern and expression position called `let` or `case` are unbound and given a new variable error status indicating that they are reserved keywords. Typing out the variables `let` or `case` and then hitting space creates a let line (and possibly an empty hole expression body if there is no line already following the let line) or a case expression, respectively.

A future refinement would include variable splitting. If I have `1|2` and hit plus, then I would get `1 + 2`. In the case that I type out a keyword, I would construct the corresponding expression, e.g., pressing space on `let|1` gives me `let _ = 1`.

title: Fix path protocol for expression lines
body:
The initial implementation of lines items https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/pull/53/files had a path protocol where an expression line and the expression had the same path. Generally we only want the cursor to be on the expression in an expression line. However, because they share the same path, when doing an action that leaves the cursor at the end of exp on an exp line, the update view code would leave the cursor at the end of the line. This would lead to issues such as the cursor inspector reporting a line item instead of type Num as expected in the following scenario:
```
1|
_
```
This PR updates the path protocol so that expressions have distinct paths from their enclosing expression lines. In the future, we may want to restructure `UHExp` and `ZExp` in order to make redundant cursor positions impossible (e.g., end of line vs end of exp line, end of opseq vs end of last exp in opseq, etc).

title: Line Items
body:
Introduces line items to Hazel programs. You can hit enter at the beginning or end of a line to create a new line. Each line may contain nothing, an expression, or a let line. Other than where an expression is expected (i.e. on the last line), lines with single empty holes are pruned and replaced with empty lines. A sequence of expressions `e1; e2; e3` is evaluated as `let _ = e1 in let _ = e2 in e3`.

![line-items](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8718124/53279832-13d06500-36d1-11e9-880c-619b43c218d5.gif)

Future refinements may include splitting of a line across two lines by hitting enter, or fusing of two lines via backspace. Need to figure out when such actions would be appropriate.

title: Coq extraction script + simple ocaml translation
body:
Ported this code from `hazel_semantics.ml`

```ocaml
  let matched_arrow ty = match ty with
    | Arrow (ty1, ty2) (* MAArr *) -> Some (ty1, ty2)
    | Hole (* MAHole *) -> Some (Hole, Hole)
    | _ -> None
```

The coq definition extracts to this:

```ocaml
  (** val matched_arrow : t -> (t, t)  option **)

  let matched_arrow = function
  | Arrow (ty1, ty2) -> Some (ty1, ty2)
  | Hole -> Some (Hole, Hole)
  | _ -> None
 end
```
